contentBlocks.text: You have a topic sentence and three supporting details. Right now they're separate ideas — today, transition words connect them into one smooth paragraph.

Transition words signal how one idea connects to the next. Some useful ones for listing details: first, next, also, in addition, finally. Watch how they smooth out a list of details: 'First, I get to run on the field. Next, I play tag with my friends. Finally, I feel less tired after moving around.' Without transitions, the same details sound choppy and disconnected. Take your three supporting details from yesterday and add a transition word to the start of each one.
Your three details now flow together as connected ideas instead of a disconnected list. Tomorrow we'll add the final piece: a concluding sentence.

objectives: Define a transition word as a word that connects one idea to the next
Add transition words to a list of supporting details to improve flow
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's 3 supporting details.
2. Read the choppy version (no transitions) aloud, then the smooth version (with transitions), and discuss the difference in how it sounds.
3. Introduce the 5 transition words: first, next, also, in addition, finally.
4. Have the child add a transition word to the start of each of their 3 details.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's topic: concluding sentences.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide the transition word list as a word bank to choose from rather than requiring recall from memory
Ready for more: ask them to try a transition word that shows a different relationship, like 'however' or 'because,' beyond just listing
Reading both versions aloud (with and without transitions) is the single most effective way to make this lesson click — don't skip it
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary based on the child's own supporting details — check that each detail now begins with an appropriate transition word (first/next/also/in addition/finally) and that the sequence makes logical sense.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Addresses Common Core Grade 4 Writing standard W.4.2c (link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases), the natural third step connecting Day 1's topic sentence to Day 2's details.
